guitar.modelsText: Fender Stratocaster "Blackie" / Gibson ES-335 / Martin acoustic
guitar.evidence: Trained knowledge: extremely well documented — "Blackie" Strat, earlier Gibson ES-335/Les Paul/SG (Cream era), Martin acoustics for Unplugged.

tone.target: dry reggae-skank clean with light breakup
tone.profile: dry reggae-skank clean with light breakup
tone.summary: A bright, dry reggae skank tone achieved with a Fender-style clean amp (US Deluxe) combined with light compression for tight attack and a subtle room reverb.

rig.name: Eric Clapton - I Shot The Sheriff - Valeton GP-180

blocks.purpose: Clean up ambient noise and tighten the percussive attack.
Enhance the initial transient attack for a tight, percussive 'skank' sound.
Provide just enough grit and warmth to define the rhythm without adding bluesy crunch.
blocks.gap: The Green OD is used lightly, mimicking a clean boost rather than heavy drive.

blocks.purpose: Emulate the bright, chimey sound of a Fender-style clean amp (Vox/Strat vibe).
Provide a bright, focused cabinet sound suitable for clean reggae tones.
Scoop the low end and boost high frequencies to enhance the 'chime' and dryness of the skank.
Kept inactive to avoid unwanted filtering or movement, but available for subtle tonal shaping if needed.
blocks.gap: The V-Wah is generally unnecessary for this specific dry reggae tone, so it is deactivated.

blocks.purpose: Deactivated to strictly avoid the 'chorus vibe' and maintain a dry sound.
Provide a subtle rhythmic echo to enhance the percussive nature without sounding wash-out.
blocks.gap: A very low mix is used, acting more like an ambient tail than a noticeable delay.

blocks.purpose: Add a light, natural room ambience as requested, keeping the sound dry but not sterile.

improvements.summary: Improve cabinet realism to better capture the bright, focused sound of a vintage Fender/Vox combo.

proposals.reason: Enhance chime and dryness for reggae skank tone.
